main_body: Stilted plank hut: a large plank-roof slab (rows 0-21) over a plank wall with a small door and a window (rows 22-36), on thin stilts
top_band: Roof slope, mid-orange plank tone with a light ridge line at rows 1-2, running down through rows ~3-19 and ending in a darker band at rows 16-19, then a dark eave at rows 20-21
evidence: The roof is a large slope that overhangs the wall and is much taller than a thin rim. It ends in a darker lower band and a dark eave line at rows 20-21 that shades the wall below. The wall is a separate vertical face, 14 rows tall. The door and window have dark inset frames. The roof is drawn with vertical plank lines and has no distinct front-edge highlight, so it is borderline, but both a roof surface and a wall face are clearly present.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tinted to the wood, which matches the reference approach. The material ramps are only about 4 steps (light orange, mid, brown, dark brown). The roof and wall use repeated vertical plank stripes with sparse grain and no per-tile highlights, speckle or varied clumps. Each tile carries only about 3-5 colours, against the references' rich tile scallops, plaster speckle and stone shading. It reads thinner and flatter than the reference houses.
